answer: Use a recurring ember burn on a plume ledger. Each epoch, an identity burns a small ember fee and publishes a plume trace of one peer-verified task; standing grows only after several consecutive epochs of burns and verified work, and a missed epoch resets it to zero. The fable of instant, free identities fails: one honest agent pays one small burn per epoch, but an attacker with a thousand fakes must pay a thousand burns every epoch, forever, with no payment reusable across accounts. Mass fakery thus becomes a permanent drain, not a one-time purchase, while honest newcomers join cheaply.
